kind: cross-validation against a mature open-source implementation (XVAL)
subject: TensorLBM :: src/tensorlbm/parallel/slab_unpacked.py (new capability, this mission) + src/tensorlbm/domain_decomposition.py (existing packed/selective convention used as control)

reference.oss_commit: 6e2c592 (cache recorded in oss_inventory.cache_commit, cached on n315/n330)
reference.oss_source_channel: oss_solutions row (repo=lbm-principles-practice/code, feature_slug=分布式多卡, tag=mpi-1d-slab-unpacked-halo-testall-overlap) + oss_inventory row (repo=lbm-principles-practice/code, status=inventoried, licence MIT, gpu field: 'MPI 1D y-slab with contiguous halo rows (no packing) + MPI_Testall overlap; OpenMP row-parallel')
oss_practice_quoted: Split NY into contiguous rank slabs with one halo row per side (halo rows allocated as rank_ny+2)
Because the layout is direction-major with contiguous y-rows, each halo block is (ndir-1)*NX contiguous doubles, so MPI_Isend/MPI_Irecv needs no packing
Call MPI_Testall after every interior y-row so the communication overlaps the remaining collision work
Combine global norms in one MPI_Allreduce over seven scalars
Ranks wrap around (rankp1/rankm1 modulo nprocs); per-rank binary shards name%0Nd_rank%d.bin, no parallel I/O
reference.zero_transcription_note: the quoted practice is read from the platform's inventoried row for that OSS commit (no retyping of code); the reference implementation itself is C++/CUDA + MPI and cannot be executed here (no mpi4py, no mpirun, no GPU: checked at run time and recorded in the report), so the REFERENCE ARM IS A SEMANTICS-EXACT TRANSPLANT, never an execution of the OSS binary. This is a comparison limit, not an upgrade.

decision: does the unpacked (no-packing) 1-D y-slab halo with Testall progress polling reproduce the single-rank solution exactly while reproducing the Taylor-Green continuum decay within the owner 15% band, and what does it cost in wire bytes / staging copies relative to the packed selective convention already in this repo?

alternatives.A1_unpacked_testall_overlap: OSS semantics: 1-D y-slab, direction-major f[q,y,x], halo block f[1:, row, :] sent straight out of the population array (zero copy), request set polled with Testall after every streamed interior row, boundary rows streamed only after completion
alternatives.A2_unpacked_blocking: same halo blocks, no overlap: waitall immediately after posting, then stream (isolates the value of the overlap)
alternatives.A3_packed_selective: in-repo convention (tensorlbm.domain_decomposition.HaloExchange semantics): only the directions that cross the face are exchanged (6 of 8 for D2Q9), packed into contiguous staging buffers
alternatives.A4_unpacked_selective: zero-copy AND selective: exchange only the crossing directions straight out of f (both savings at once) - not an OSS practice, included to price the OSS trade-off

hypothesis.H1: decomposition neutrality: every arm at NP=2 and NP=4 reproduces the NP=1 single-rank solution to round-off (max|u-u_ref|/max|u_ref| < 1e-12)
hypothesis.H2: physical accuracy: the Taylor-Green probe amplitude and the field L2 error stay below the owner 15% band against the continuum solution at the acceptance grid
hypothesis.H3: testall overlap never changes the result (A1 == A2 exactly) and reduces wall time at NP>1
hypothesis.H4: the OSS unpacked full-block convention costs exactly 8/6 = +33.3% wire bytes versus the selective convention, and saves exactly two staging memcpys per face per step (A3 staging bytes > 0, A1 staging bytes == 0)
hypothesis.H0_falsifier: any identity deviation >= 1e-12, any physics error >= 15%, or any H4 byte/copy count off the closed-form value

metrics.identity_maxrel: max_y,x |u_arm - u_NP1| / max|u_NP1| on the full global field after the predeclared step count
metrics.probe_rel_err_pct: 100 * |u_x(0,0) - u0 exp(-2 nu k^2 t)| / |u0 exp(-2 nu k^2 t)|, the primary physics KPI
metrics.wire_bytes_per_step: bytes moved per step per rank, closed form 4 * ndir_x * NX * 8 (2 sends + 2 receives), ndir_x = 8 unpacked / 6 selective
metrics.staging_bytes_per_step: bytes moved by explicit staging memcpy per step (packing)
metrics.messages_per_step: Isend+Irecv count per step per rank (4: two faces, send and receive)
metrics.testall_polls_per_step: Testall calls per step actually executed (overlap on) - the progress-polling cost
metrics.mlups: NX*NY*steps / wall_s / 1e6 for the whole job (all ranks), the throughput KPI
metrics.mass_drift_rel: |sum(rho) - N| / N from the single per-window Allreduce of seven scalars
metrics.ma_max: max|u| / cs, must stay < 0.1 (incompressible LBM regime)

unit_of_analysis: one completed run (arm x NP) at fixed grid, tau, u0 and step count; KPIs are scalars on the global reconstructed field

baseline_control.representation_control: A_ref = A1 at NP=1 (no transport at all: the halo is a periodic in-memory self-wrap), so any deviation at NP>1 is a decomposition/transport error and nothing else
baseline_control.physics_baseline: continuum Taylor-Green vortex ux = u0 cos(kx)cos(ky)exp(-2 nu k^2 t), uy = -u0 sin(kx)sin(ky)exp(-2 nu k^2 t), k = 2 pi / NX, one wavelength per box, periodic in both directions
baseline_control.convention_control: A3/A4 differ from A1 ONLY in which directions are exchanged and whether a staging copy is made - same collision, same streaming order, same time integration

predeclared_thresholds.interpretation: H1/H3 hold iff every NP>1 arm matches NP=1 within 1e-12 relative (nine orders stricter than the owner band: a decomposition change must be exact, only the physics-vs-continuum comparison uses the 15% band). H2 uses the acceptance grid N=128; coarser grids are reported as convergence evidence, never as a pass.
predeclared_thresholds.stability_rule: a run producing a non-finite population, rho outside [0.95, 1.05] or max|u| > 0.1 cs is declared failed and reported, never tuned away
predeclared_thresholds.stopping_rule: every arm runs the step count fixed before the run (600 at N=128); the step count is NOT extended after looking at a KPI. Wall budget 600 s per arm, above which the arm moves to the cluster queue

variables_changed: transport scheme: unpacked full block (OSS) / unpacked selective / packed selective (repo)
overlap: Testall progress polling vs blocking waitall
Testall polling granularity: every 1 / 8 / 64 streamed rows
resolution: N = 64, 128 at equal physical decay time
variables_held_fixed: Taylor-Green initial condition u0 = 0.04, one wavelength per box, periodic x and y
pull streaming, two ghost rows per slab, ranks wrap modulo nprocs
step count per grid (600 at N=128) and the seven-scalar Allreduce window
confounders: no MPI stack in the image (no mpi4py, no mpirun) -> ranks are OS threads and the wire is an in-process queue: the byte counts are exact but the wall times are not MI times, and the GIL damps the overlap benefit (A2/A1 speedup is a LOWER bound on a real MPI run)
the shim copies every payload, i.e. it pays exactly the staging memcpy the unpacked scheme avoids on a real wire, so A1's copy advantage is not visible in these timings

continuum Taylor-Green is not the exact discrete solution: the residual error is a lattice/Ma error of the LBM scheme itself, not a decomposition error, which is why the identity KPI (1e-12) and the physics KPI (15%) are kept separate
the NP=1 arm has no transport, so its wall time is not comparable to NP>1 (used only as the identity reference)

environment.ranks: OS threads inside one process, one directed queue.Queue per (rank, rank) direction

analysis: grouped by arm; no outlier removal; identity errors are relative to the NP=1 field, physics errors relative to the continuum solution at the same time; the two sensitivity tables (poll granularity, grid convergence) are reported separately and are not acceptance criteria
fail_stage_plan: fail_stage in {transport, halo_block, stream_row, physics, kpi_analysis} with failure_reason carrying the measured deviation
